subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steering as boundary-based behavior, or add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, channel UX, Codex app-server integration, fallback behavior, and whether this becomes a default behavior or an opt-in mode/config surface.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use narrower issues only to ensure messages reach existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle after maintainer-approved upgrade proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior maintainer-labeled replacement PR and active-run steering discussion point to vincentkoc as the strongest owner for the shared queue/runtime decision.
